title: Bitcoin's Expected Return: An Age Rule That Beats Current Practice: paper and replication package
description: Working paper and full replication package. Backtest of the ways practitioners set Bitcoin's long-run expected return (constant rates of 7-21% a year, Bitcoin's own past growth, trend models, a CAPM rate) against the returns that followed over rolling three- to five-year periods since 2012, with gold as a control and Ether as a younger comparison. An age rule implicit in Bitcoin's power-law price trend (exponent divided by age) comes closest, forecasting about 32% a year for 2026-2031. Includes all data, scripts, result tables and figures; the scripts reproduce every number in the paper.
